MAIN THEOREM AND CONSEQUENCE

There is a stationary irreducible finite all-even CTMC, with positive finite entropy production and six deterministic observed labels, whose observed path law P has all of the following properties:
  (a) P is exactly invariant under ordinary time reversal;
  (b) EVERY finite reflected future/past probability kernel, at arbitrary times and including the reflection boundary, is classically completely positive, with a single common ten-atom nonnegative factorization;
  (c) its observable reflection Hilbert space has finite rank eight and a self-adjoint positive contraction semigroup;
  (d) nevertheless P is outside the rational-cylinder closure of observations of ALL finite stationary reversible CTMCs, with no bounds on hidden dimension, rates, activity, stationary masses, or reducibility.

Thus even globally compatible complete positivity of every reflected word table does not characterize hidden equilibrium. A genuine positive common semigroup/detailed-balance obstruction survives ALL reflection CP tests, not merely individual pair/covariance tests. The construction uses a nonreducing observable subspace: the forward generator is invariant and self-adjoint there, while the adjoint leaks out of that subspace.

A general rigidity theorem below also gives a necessary-and-sufficient observable characterization of equilibrium closure for a finite-rank class whose static positive factors are forced onto finitely many state vectors. In that class equilibrium closure equals exact finite reversible realizability, and a finite nonnegative edge-flow linear program decides the remaining compatibility once the forced vectors/weights are known. This is a subclass characterization, not a universal solution for arbitrary path laws.

Append-only addendum to v2. Status: internally derived exact fixed-lag certificate and scoped internal mathematical review. No external validation or priority claim.

1. TYPOGRAPHIC CLARIFICATION
Some v1/v2 formulas use two adjacent greater-than characters: one closes the inner-product angle bracket, and the other starts >=. They mean NONNEGATIVITY, not equality. The fixed-frame Farkas criterion is
  sum_i pi_i inner(Z_i,A x_i) >= 0
for every field with
  inner(Z_i-Z_j,x_i-x_j) >= 0 for all i,j.
All uses of this criterion in the proof and the negative witness have this meaning. This is a notation clarification, not a change of theorem.

2. EXPLICIT FIXED RATIONAL LAG
Retain the v2 exact ten-state Q, feature matrix H with rows xi_i, field Z_i and observable generator L with QH=HL. Define
  F(t)=(1/10)sum_i Z_i dot[xi_i-xi_i exp(tL)].
Since exp(tQ)H=H exp(tL), the same function is
  F(t)=(1/10)sum_i sum_k Z_i[k] (H[i,k]-(exp(tQ)H)[i,k]).
Every feature column has supremum norm <=1. Exact Fraction arithmetic verifies
  ||Q||_infinity <=2,
  beta=(1/10)sum_i ||Z_i||_1 <=2.
Let delta=-F'(0)>0, exactly
  delta=3230342770615041346411154110862042812888496486195459
     /540482346568300350932733621017587377233567340000000000
     =0.005976777578630545... .

For 0<t<1/2, the matrix-exponential Taylor remainder gives
  |F(t)-tF'(0)|
   <= beta [exp(||Q||_infinity t)-1-||Q||_infinity t]
   <=2 [exp(2t)-1-2t]
   <=4t^2/(1-2t).
The last inequality follows by summing the series and using k!>=2 for k>=2.

Choose t=1/1000. Then
  F(1/1000) <=-delta/1000+1/249500
             =-530976349400304929993698659284984609164225066611534041
               /269700690937581875115434076887776101239550102660000000000000
             <-0.000001968761 .
Thus the symmetric-coupling monotonicity condition already fails at one explicitly named finite positive lag. It is unnecessary to leave that lag existential or to take derivatives of any approximating hidden generators.
